title: Military Leadership Competencies
source: 2. Military Leadership Competencies (Leading, Developing, and Achieving).pptx

questions.stem: Which of the following defines leadership?
questions.key: The process of influencing men providing purpose, direction and motivation to accomplish a mission and improve the organization
distractors: The ability to do something successfully or efficiently
The central, innermost, or most essential part of anything
The one that leads or guides a group, organization, or country
questions.explanation: The deck defines leadership as the process of influencing people by providing purpose, direction and motivation to accomplish the mission and improve the organization.
why: That is the definition of competency, not of leadership.
That is the definition of core, one word in the term core leader competency.
That is the definition of a leader, the person who leads.

questions.stem: A leader provides purpose, motivation and inspiration, enforces standards, and balances the mission with the welfare of soldiers. Under the Leading competency, this describes which subset?
distractors: Extends influence beyond the chain of command
questions.explanation: Slide 21 lists providing purpose, motivation and inspiration, enforcing standards, and balancing mission and welfare of soldiers as the parts of leads others.
why: Leads by example is displaying character and demonstrating competence.
Communicates is listening actively, stating goals for action and ensuring shared understanding.
Extends influence beyond the chain of command is building trust outside the chain, knowing the limits of influence, and negotiating.

questions.stem: It is the competency that focuses on who is being led and with what degree of authority and influence.
questions.explanation: The Leading competency has four subsets and addresses who is being led and the degree of authority and influence, including two ways leaders convey influence.
why: Developing is about leaving the organization better and preparing self and others.
Achieving is about direction, planning and accomplishing missions.
Leadership is the overall process of influencing people, not one of the three competencies.

questions.stem: Which list contains the four subsets of the Leading competency?
questions.key: Leads others, extends influence beyond the chain of command, leads by example, communicates
distractors: Leads others, prepares self, leads by example, communicates
Leads others, extends influence beyond the chain of command, develops others, communicates
Extends influence beyond the chain of command, leads by example, communicates, accomplishes missions
questions.explanation: The Leading competency comprises leads others, extends influence beyond the chain of command, leads by example, and communicates.
why: Prepares self belongs to the Developing competency.
Develops others belongs to the Developing competency.
Accomplishes missions belongs to the Achieving competency, and leads others is missing.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes the Developing competency?
questions.key: Good leaders strive to leave an organization better than they found it and work on their own development for new challenges
distractors: It begins in the short term by setting objectives and in the long term rests on a clear vision
It focuses on who is being led and with what degree of authority and influence
It focuses on structuring what needs to be done to get results
questions.explanation: The Developing competency is described as leaders striving to leave an organization better than they found it while also working on their own development to prepare for new challenges.
why: That describes the Achieving competency.
That describes the Leading competency.
Structuring what needs to be done to get results describes the Achieving competency.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes the Achieving competency?
questions.key: It begins in the short term by setting objectives and in the long term rests on a clear vision
distractors: Good leaders strive to leave an organization better than they found it
It addresses two ways by which leaders convey influence
Leaders create a positive environment, prepare self and develop others
questions.explanation: Achieving starts with short-term objectives and, over the long term, is based on a clear vision; it covers getting results and organizing how to achieve them.
why: That is the idea behind the Developing competency.
Conveying influence belongs to the Leading competency.
Positive environment, prepare self and develop others are the three Developing subsets.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a subset of the Leading competency?
distractors: Extends influence beyond the chain of command
questions.explanation: Prepares self is a subset of the Developing competency. The Leading competency has four subsets: leads others, extends influence beyond the chain of command, leads by example, and communicates.
why: Leads by example is one of the four Leading subsets.
Communicates is one of the four Leading subsets.
Extending influence beyond the chain of command is one of the four Leading subsets.

questions.stem: A company commander consistently displays character and demonstrates competence so that soldiers can see the standard in action. Under the Leading competency, this describes which subset?
distractors: Extends influence beyond the chain of command
questions.explanation: Displaying character and demonstrating competence are the two parts of the leads by example subset.
why: Leads others covers providing purpose, motivation and inspiration, enforcing standards, and balancing mission and soldier welfare.
Communicates covers listening actively, stating goals for action and ensuring shared understanding.
Extending influence covers building trust outside the chain of command and negotiating or resolving conflict.

questions.stem: A leader listens actively, states goals for action, and makes sure everyone shares the same understanding of the task. Under the Leading competency, this describes which subset?
distractors: Extends influence beyond the chain of command
questions.explanation: Listening actively, stating goals for action and ensuring shared understanding are the three parts of the communicates subset.
why: Leads by example is about displaying character and demonstrating competence.
Leads others is about purpose and motivation, standards, and mission versus welfare.
Extending influence is about trust, influence limits and negotiation outside the chain of command.

questions.stem: A company commander builds trust with another unit outside her chain of command, recognizes the limits of her influence, and negotiates to resolve a conflict over shared resources. Which subset of the Leading competency does this describe?
questions.key: Extends influence beyond the chain of command
questions.explanation: Building trust outside the chain of command, understanding the sphere, means and limits of influence, and negotiating, consensus building and conflict resolution make up this subset.
why: Leads others concerns those within the leader's own authority, such as enforcing standards.
Leads by example is about displaying character and demonstrating competence.
Communicates is about active listening, stating goals and shared understanding.

questions.stem: It is the ability to do something successfully or efficiently.
questions.explanation: The deck defines competency as the ability to do something successfully or efficiently.
why: Leadership is the process of influencing people to accomplish a mission and improve the organization.
Core leader competency adds the idea of the most essential ability of a person who leads.
A leader is the one who leads or guides, not an ability.
